1.label: Curative intent — comparative evidence is specific to the studied population and endpoint

2.label: Curative-intent alternative — when resection / transplant / ablation not feasible

3.label: Bridge, downstage or conversion to surgery/LT, or adjunct to surgery

4.label: Selected disease control or palliation — sequencing and benefit vary by tumour and modality

pcca|abl.head: No established percutaneous thermal ablation role

roles.when: Central bile ducts and adjacent vessels limit safe margins. Endobiliary RFA is a separate palliative technique. Review transplant candidacy before intervention; protect the hilar ducts and vasculature. The explicit OPTN primary-tumour biopsy prohibition must not be generalized to every procedure.
ev: Primary hilar duct disease differs from mass-forming iCCA.

pcca|sbrt.head: Protocol RT before LT; selected non-LT control

roles.when: Curative-intent LT pathway: follow the approved neoadjuvant protocol, then operative staging and LT. OPTN 9.5.A requires neoadjuvant therapy, not a specific RT technique or Mayo regimen. Chemotherapy-only selection remains a protocol-level decision.
ev: 287 enrolled; 5-year intention-to-treat overall survival 53% from start of therapy; 5-year post-transplant recurrence-free survival 65%. No isolated RT effect.
17 evaluated; 12 RT-treated (11 SBRT), 9 listed, 6 LT. SBRT 50–60 Gy/3–5 fx; 1-y post-LT OS 83%.
26 LT recipients: 12 GemCis-only vs 14 RT-containing. No significant OS/RFS difference; no equivalence or ITT benefit established.
49 LT recipients, 27 neoadjuvant chemoradiation vs 22 no neoadjuvant therapy. Lower adjusted recurrence hazard, more vascular complications; no proven OS benefit or equivalence.

roles.when: Unresectable pCCA outside LT: NCCN lists chemoradiation with or without sequential chemotherapy as an option, without requiring prior systemic control (v1.2026, original PDF p23, EXTRA-1). BSG supports selected SBRT/PBT after systemic therapy. Individualize in MDT; trial preferred. No proven routine survival advantage; drainage and organ-at-risk constraints govern feasibility.
ev: 6 patients, 60 Gy/15 fractions; 1-y LC 80% from RT. Grade 3 cholangitis in 5/6; no randomized survival benefit. No dose-limiting toxicity used grade ≥4 hepatobiliary or grade ≥3 gastrointestinal criteria; grade 3 cholangitis was not a DLT.
ASCO 2024 abstract 4006. n=69, 84% perihilar. PFS 8.6 vs 9.0 months, HR 1.00; no significant OS benefit. DOI 10.1200/JCO.2024.42.16_suppl.4006
Supports consideration of SBRT/PBT after systemic therapy; benefit evidence limited.
Phase II target n=30; protocol, not outcome evidence.
19/41 plans deviated from protocol objectives, mostly reduced PTV coverage to respect duodenal or gastric constraints. Does not establish efficacy.
Contouring and planning variability study (one benchmark case, 6 centres), not patient survival or local-control results.

roles.when: Post-resection: NCCN lists chemoradiation for R1 or node-positive eCCA and as a nonpreferred option for R0/node-negative disease (v1.2026, original PDF p24, EXTRA-2). Systemic therapy and clinical trial are preferred. BSG specifically supports R1 discussion. No pCCA-specific randomized proof of RT survival benefit.
ev: Shared decision about potential local benefit and toxicity; no pCCA-specific randomized proof.

pcca|y90.head: No established routine role for primary pCCA

roles.when: Do not extrapolate iCCA radioembolization series to infiltrative hilar duct tumors. Any liver-parenchymal target requires individualized MDT review and biliary safety assessment. Review transplant candidacy before intervention; protect the hilar ducts and vasculature. The explicit OPTN primary-tumour biopsy prohibition must not be generalized to every procedure.
ev: Primary hilar duct disease differs from mass-forming iCCA.

pcca|tace.head: No established routine role for primary pCCA

roles.when: No curative or standard sequencing evidence for the primary hilar tumor. Obstruction, biliary instrumentation and infection heighten concern. Review transplant candidacy before intervention; protect the hilar ducts and vasculature. The explicit OPTN primary-tumour biopsy prohibition must not be generalized to every procedure.
ev: Primary hilar duct disease differs from mass-forming iCCA.

pcca|hai.head: HAIC evidence is exploratory and regimen-specific

roles.when: Chinese trial tested radiation-emitting vs conventional stents, BOTH with arterial gemcitabine/cisplatin. It did not test HAIC versus systemic therapy or pump FUDR.
ev: 126 patients; OS 10.2 vs 6.7 months. Effect is the stent comparison within HAIC, not proof of HAI benefit.

pcca|htx.head: No established primary hilar treatment role

roles.when: No pCCA-specific curative, survival or transplant-bridge evidence. Central hilar anatomy requires research-protocol assessment. Review transplant candidacy before intervention; protect the hilar ducts and vasculature. The explicit OPTN primary-tumour biopsy prohibition must not be generalized to every procedure.
ev: Primary hilar duct disease differs from mass-forming iCCA.

summary: Randomized comparisons support ablation for selected small HCC and CRLM. A nonsignificant difference does not establish equivalence: read each trial’s population, endpoint and limits.
SBRT (HCC ≤5 cm, CRLM 1–3 lesions, iCCA at BED >80 Gy); Y-90 segmentectomy (solitary HCC ≤8 cm); ablation for iCCA ≤3 cm and limited NELM.
HCC: bridge/downstage to LT; adjuvant HAIC, TACE or RT; neoadjuvant RT for PVTT; TAE then staged resection for rupture. HAI adjuvant/conversion in CRLM and iCCA. Y-90 radiation lobectomy for FLR.
TACE standard for BCLC-B and NELM; Y-90 for refractory CRLM and bulky NELM; HAIC for advanced HCC; TACE / HAI for unresectable iCCA; single-fraction RT for liver pain.
Histotripsy for all tumours; SBRT and HAI in NELM; Y-90 1st-line in CRLM.
notes: Resection and liver transplantation remain the reference standard; tiers describe each modality's role relative to them.
Cell colour = principal role; tagged lines = other evidence-supported roles. Numbers in boxes are PubMed IDs.
*RETNET results presented at NANETS 2025 (abstract); not yet PubMed-indexed — PMID shown is the protocol.

Abbrev.: LT liver transplant; LC local control; LTP local tumour progression; FFLP freedom from local progression; MVI macrovascular invasion; PVTT portal vein tumour thrombus; EHD extrahepatic disease; BED biologically effective dose; FLR future liver remnant; DCR disease control rate; HE hepatic encephalopathy.

15 October 2026 HAI update: Dutch adjuvant PUMP (ASCO LBA3506), US EA2222 (NCT05863195, unresectable CRLM) and iCCA PUMP-2 are distinct trials. Lecture and published PUMP analyses differ; this matrix uses the published abstract. HAI does not establish MELD exception or LT eligibility. Shared programme safeguards: PMIDs 39962001, 36346892, 24154839.

23 October 2026: pCCA added separately from iCCA. Endobiliary RFA, PDT and radiation-emitting stents are reviewed below as biliary-directed techniques. No standalone local modality has established curative equivalence to resection or protocol LT for primary pCCA. Proposed institutional interpretation remains subject to MDT ratification.

ABCDE review, 23 October 2026: tiers describe clinical intent, not guaranteed cure, a formal evidence grade, or approval. Read each endpoint and time origin. pCCA RT may support protocol LT or selected local control; RT is not specifically mandated by OPTN. Clinical benefit, allocation eligibility and institutional approval are separate. Other tumour selection criteria were not expanded by this pCCA review.

Neoadjuvant therapy then LT for locally advanced iCCA (prospective series); liver-directed therapy as a bridge in either pathway is untested

pCCA: resection for resectable disease; approved neoadjuvant-to-LT pathway for selected unresectable disease. Both have curative intent; LT superiority over resection is not established. Transplant review before primary-tumour transperitoneal biopsy.
